disclaimer: Starter comparison baseline with a small number of entries. It is not a statute, not a court ruling, and not a statement that any clause is legal or illegal. Jurisdiction-specific enforceability should be reviewed by a qualified legal professional.

entries.title: Salary
entries.standard_expectation: The agreement should state the salary as an amount and say when it is paid.
entries.comparison_guidance: A stated salary and pay date match this standard.
entries.financial_basis: Salary is an input to formulas such as months of salary.
entries.suggested_revision: The employee shall receive a stated monthly salary, paid on a stated day each month.
entries.negotiation_goal: Keep the salary and pay date explicit.
entries.why_it_matters: Other clauses convert months of salary into rupees only if the salary is stated.
entries.source_notes: ClauseLens starter comparison baseline. Not a legal requirement.

entries.title: Payment in lieu of notice
entries.standard_expectation: If the employee leaves without serving notice, any payment in lieu should not exceed salary for the unserved part of the stated notice period.
expected_elements: A link to the notice period
A cap equal to the unserved notice
missing_elements: Cap tied to the unserved notice period

element_checks.description: Payment is limited to the unserved notice period

entries.comparison_guidance: Flag a payment in lieu of notice that is a fixed multiple of salary larger than the notice period.
entries.financial_basis: Exposure is the stated multiple times the monthly salary. Python multiplies those figures.
entries.suggested_revision: If the employee does not serve the full notice period, the employee shall pay salary for the unserved days of notice only.
entries.negotiation_goal: Tie any payment in lieu of notice to the unserved notice days.
entries.why_it_matters: A fixed multiple of salary can exceed the notice period itself.
entries.source_notes: ClauseLens starter comparison baseline. Not a legal requirement.

entries.title: Non-compete
entries.standard_expectation: Any post-employment restriction should be limited in time, geography, and scope.
entries.comparison_guidance: Flag a restriction that is worldwide or lasts several years.
entries.financial_basis: A restriction on future work has no rupee figure in the agreement. Exposure is unknown.
entries.suggested_revision: For six months after leaving, the employee shall not solicit the employer's clients with whom the employee worked directly.
entries.negotiation_goal: Narrow the restriction to a short, specific non-solicitation.
entries.why_it_matters: A broad restriction can limit future work, and its cost cannot be calculated from the agreement.
entries.source_notes: ClauseLens starter comparison baseline. Not a legal requirement.

entries.title: Final settlement timeline
entries.standard_expectation: The agreement should say when final salary and other dues are paid after the employee leaves.
entries.comparison_guidance: Treat the settlement timeline as missing when the agreement never states it.
entries.financial_basis: No separate amount is invented for a missing timeline.
entries.suggested_revision: Final salary and other dues shall be paid within 30 days of the employee's last working day.
entries.negotiation_goal: Add a date for the final settlement.
entries.why_it_matters: The agreement does not say when final dues are paid.
entries.source_notes: ClauseLens starter comparison baseline. The 30-day wording is a proposed revision, not a legal requirement.
